newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Lagoven can meet contracts for part of November.
newsitem.headline: Lagoven can meet contracts for part of November.

text.p: Lagoven, affiliate of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela, is making arrangements to meet supply contracts for October and "a good part of November" to make up for lost output while the catalytic cracker at its Amuay refinery is repaired, a company spokesman said Friday.
"Lagoven has a level of stocks to cover October and a good part of November," the company spokesman said, citing information supplied by Lagoven's commercial department.
Lagoven is making arrangements with other Petroleos de Venezuela (PDVSA) units, "to make available certain amounts of gasoline to meet the most immediate shipments," the spokesman said.
The extra gasoline would come from Maraven's Cardon refinery, Corpoven's El Palito refinery and PDVSA's Isla refinery in Curacao, he said.

The extent to which these arrangements will be able to continue meeting arranged contracts depends on how long it takes to fix a compressor in the catalytic cracker at the 510,000 barrels per day Amuay refinery, he added.
"Everything depends on how long it takes to start up the cracker," he said.
Lagoven announced on Wednesday that repairs of the cracker would take about three weeks.
